title: The bag that would not loop
scenario:
A coffee roaster approved one still of its new bag: the approved still. It shows the front of the bag next to a steaming cup. Your teammate planned three clips from it and sent you the plan before running anything.

Use the exhibit. The field names and rules are from Luma's, Google's and Runway's docs (October 2026). The brand, the files and the plan are made up for this case.
exhibit:
CLIP 1: WEB HEADER LOOP (Luma, made up)
  model:              ray-3.2
  type:               video
  video.duration:     10s
  video.start_frame:  bag-front.png
  video.end_frame:    bag-front.png
  video.loop:         true
  prompt: "Slow dolly in toward the bag."

CLIP 2: SOCIAL CLIP (Gemini Omni Flash, made up)
  input:  bag-front.png
  prompt: "Make it move."

CLIP 3: PRODUCT TURN (made up)
  Plan: a full 360-degree turn of the bag.
  Approved stills: bag-front.png only.

questions.prompt: Luma would refuse the Clip 1 request. What should it look like instead?

options.text: start_frame only, loop true, and a 5-second duration
options.explanation: Right. Luma rejects loop with 10s and with end_frame. A start frame, loop: true and 5 seconds is a valid loop from the still.

options.text: start_frame and end_frame kept, loop removed, 10s
options.explanation: Luma does not take start or end frames with 10s. Without loop: true, Luma does not promise a seamless loop.

options.text: keyframes at 0 and 120 instead, with loop still on
options.explanation: The Luma docs say keyframes is mutually exclusive with start_frame, end_frame and loop.

options.text: No change, because Luma fixes these settings itself
options.explanation: Luma refuses a request that breaks its rules. It does not fix them for you.

questions.prompt: Even as a valid request, Clip 1's prompt is a poor fit for a loop. Why?

options.text: A dolly in ends closer than it starts, so each repeat jumps back
options.explanation: Right. A loop must end where it began. A camera that travels toward the bag cannot do that (our advice).

options.text: A dolly in is too slow, so a loop must use a fast whip pan instead
options.explanation: A whip pan is also a move that ends somewhere else. Speed is not the problem; the end point is.

options.text: A dolly in needs a person in the frame, and the still has nobody
options.explanation: A dolly moves the camera. It needs no person in the shot.

options.text: A dolly in is not a camera move that video models can understand
options.explanation: Chapter 1 shows dolly in vendor prompt examples. The issue here is the loop, not the word.

options.text: "Make it move a lot more. Make it look really good."
options.explanation: Still vague. The Gemini API docs say vague prompts like make it move give weaker results than detailed motion.

options.text: "Use the image as a loose idea. Invent a new bag design."
options.explanation: The bag is approved. A new design throws away what the client signed off.

options.text: "Use this image as the starting frame. Steam rises slowly."
options.explanation: Right. On Omni the model decides how to use the image unless you say it. Then describe the motion.

options.text: "Show the bag. Let the model choose all of the motion."
options.explanation: This gives no motion and no role for the image. On Omni the model then decides both.

questions.prompt: Only the front of the bag is approved. What do you do about the 360-degree turn?

options.text: Run it as planned, because the model can see the back in the still
options.explanation: A front-only still does not show the back. In our reading, the model has to invent it.

options.text: Get side and back views approved first, or make the turn a small arc
options.explanation: Right. Runway's tips ask for front, back and side references. Without them, keep the move small (our advice).

options.text: Write the back of the bag in words, because text is more exact here
options.explanation: Words leave the back to the model's guess. Approved images hold the look better.

options.text: Turn on loop, because a looping clip shows the bag from all sides
options.explanation: A loop repeats a clip. It does not show sides that no image or prompt gave.
